newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates steady to lower.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were steady to slightly lower amid high kuna liquidity on Tuesday morning, dealers said.

"The morning's trade started with an exceptionally high supply of kuna funds, the demand falling far below it," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters, adding that there was a very large surplus of 40 million kuna.
Fresh loans totalled 15.4 million kuna. Of this, 11.6 million were call money loans struck mostly at 10.5 percent, though some creditors granted funds even at 9.5 percent.
The rest were term loans, granted at 12.5 and 16 percent.
Due to high liquidity none of 68 banks operating in Croatia had shortfalls on Monday night, so there was no overnight trade. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
